title: Good Dog Shift
hook: Keep a small dog daycare happy by throwing toys, maintaining activities and finding the right moment to give each personality a rest.
audience: Pet-simulation and active management players who enjoy expressive creatures and juggling needs.
core_loop: Accept a small group; move an attendant and aim throws; refill activities and water; manage play, attention and rest; choose one equipment improvement between short shifts.
score_notes: See management-trends.md. Six to seven days is a conditional upper end; four days is not credible from scratch.

inspiration.connection: Enrichment activities inspire the creature behaviours and hands-on service, without copying a branded toy or claiming real training advice.
inspiration.evergreen_promise: Readable personalities, humorous reactions and balancing competing needs remain appealing beyond the product trend.
inspiration.current_timing: Historical source growth or current expansion is recorded separately; September search slope and future peak are unverified.

commercial_hypothesis.condition: Genre/price evidence and a worthwhile finished experience within the work budget are both required. These are test prices, not selected prices or sales forecasts.

prototype_envelope.scope: One-day slice with three dogs, one toy and one rest zone. Continue only if four of five available target players predict two different reactions and three deliberately alter play/rest or toy use to resolve a conflict and choose another shift. Hold if dogs feel like status bars or convincing reactions require a much larger animation system.

production_envelope.scope: One 2D yard with fixed zones, three fictional temperaments, fetch plus two activity stations and a rest area, three shifts with seeded dog arrivals, simple upgrades and local save.
production_envelope.note: Includes prototype, original modest art/audio, finite content, controls/settings/save, packaged Windows QA and draft store media. Calendar onboarding/review, recruitment and unforeseen rework are separate. Estimate is not demonstrated.

cash_assumptions.note: Existing tools assumed. No purchases or cash allocation. Steam fee and optional assets remain separate planning inputs in the run.

support_estimate: Allow 1–2 owner hours for launch-month triage/review, plus agent fixes as needed; actual burden unknown.

evidence.claim: August 27, 2026 US retail article reports electronic pet toys +27% year over year and treat-dispensing toys +15%; exact endpoint and unit-versus-value basis unspecified.
Updated July 13, 2026: table reports private dog park searches +50% over one year and lick mat +21%. Geography/endpoints incomplete and internal inconsistencies in other entries limit confidence.
Pupper park: USD 2.99 regular/current, 38 Steam-purchase reviews, 86.8% positive; developer positions a 15–30-minute play session.
To The Rescue!: USD 19.99 regular/current, 1,864 reviews, 66.1% positive. Larger dog-care management reference above ceiling; causes of mixed reception not investigated.
Minami Lane developer's USD 4.99 / 50,000 first-month sales postmortem supports the wider small-management audience, not direct demand for this dog loop or few-day feasibility.

risks: The close low-priced Pupper park has only 38 Steam-purchase reviews.
To The Rescue! has mixed response at a higher price; pet appeal alone is insufficient.
Dog pathing, expressive animation and legible needs are core costs.
Retail enrichment growth is not PC game purchase intent.
evidence_limits: Desk research only. No own playable build, competitor hands-on test, measured organic conversion, target-player willingness to pay or validated production time. Current names are working titles without clearance.
next_test: One-day slice with three dogs, one toy and one rest zone. Continue only if four of five available target players predict two different reactions and three deliberately alter play/rest or toy use to resolve a conflict and choose another shift. Hold if dogs feel like status bars or convincing reactions require a much larger animation system.
decision_reason: Shortlisted for a hands-on pet simulation choice; charming reactions are the central unproved production dependency.

decision_history.reason: Shortlisted for a hands-on pet simulation choice; charming reactions are the central unproved production dependency. Research only; no game selected.
